topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations and the cellular origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose progression depends on their genetic and cellular context.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and their contribution to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how strongly environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than cancer arising solely through chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the general argument through a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, including the metabolic processes that determine their activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and conclude the preceding account of carcinogen mechanisms.

topics.label: Evidence of carcinogen exposure in human populations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from people can connect carcinogen exposure to cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental tests of carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how experimental model systems test carcinogenic potential and why their results may not capture human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions and frames everyday exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
